result:
All 76 test methods across the three classes pass.

I created three self-contained JUnit 5 test classes under `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/reflect/`:

- **`ConstructorUtilsAgentTest`** — covers `getAccessibleConstructor` (by types and by `Constructor`), `getMatchingAccessibleConstructor` (exact/assignable/varargs/no-match), `invokeConstructor`/`invokeExactConstructor` (happy path, no-such-method, abstract class, wrapped exceptions, exact-match-only for `invokeExactConstructor`), null-argument boundary cases, and the deprecated public no-arg constructor.
- **`MemberUtilsAgentTest`** — covers `isPublic`, `isStatic`, `isAccessible`, `isPackage`, `isMatchingConstructor`/`isMatchingMethod` (exact, varargs, null-params), `compareConstructorFit`/`compareMethodFit`, and `setAccessibleWorkaround` (package-private declaring class vs. public class vs. null).
- **`MethodUtilsAgentTest`** — covers `getAccessibleMethod` (all overloads), `getMatchingAccessibleMethod`, `getMatchingMethod` (including empty-name/null-class errors), `getMethodObject`, `getMethodsListWithAnnotation`/`getMethodsWithAnnotation`, `getOverrideHierarchy`, `getAnnotation`, and `invokeMethod`/`invokeStaticMethod`/`invokeExactMethod`/`invokeExactStaticMethod` (varargs, forced-access to private methods, wrapped target exceptions, null-object/no-such-method errors).

No lambdas, diamond operators, or underscored numeric literals were used (per the `--release 8` constraint), using anonymous `Executable` implementations for `assertThrows` instead. All fixtures are nested inside the respective test files, so each test class remains self-contained.
